experience.label: Background
experience.title: Agency Experience from the Field
paragraphs: Before going independent, I spent two years as a developer at a digital agency in Vienna. There I worked on live web and app projects – including applications with hundreds of thousands of active users.

That gave me insight into both the technical side and the reality of agency projects: existing codebases, deadlines, reviews, client feedback, changing requirements, and collaboration within a development team.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Working Together

items.question: Can you get up to speed in an existing codebase?
items.answer: Yes. Support can explicitly take place within existing projects. At the start we clarify architecture, coding conventions, existing documentation and the definition of done.

items.question: Do you also take on individual features?
items.answer: Yes. The collaboration doesn't have to cover a whole project. Clearly scoped features, integrations, bug fixes or design-to-code tasks are also possible.

items.question: Do you work directly with our development team?
items.answer: Yes. I can integrate into existing development processes and work with tickets, Git, pull requests and code reviews, for example.

items.question: Can you implement existing Figma designs?
items.answer: Yes. Design-to-code is part of my offering. Existing designs can be integrated responsively and component-based into the existing application.

items.question: Which technologies do you cover?
items.answer: My focus is on React, Next.js, TypeScript as well as Flutter and Dart. Depending on the project, I also work with existing APIs, backend services and cloud solutions.

items.question: Is short-notice support possible?
items.answer: Depending on current availability, yes. Scope, timeframe and required capacity are best clarified right at the start.

items.question: How is billing handled?
items.answer: Depending on scope, the collaboration can be billed hourly, via an agreed retainer, or on a project basis.

items.question: Is working in the background / white label possible?
items.answer: Working in the background or as part of the existing project team is possible by arrangement.
